dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Systematically inspected all five files up front: recorded exact sizes for every graph (DM 7937/34753, HS 13276/110528, y2kr 2379/16063, SC 5831/77149), confirmed reference alignment format and verified its 2379 lines match the y2kr node count.

Quantified the baseline: computed that the provided reference alignment itself scores only S3=0.248 against the yeast target of 0.55 — establishing what a naive/perfect-NC mapping achieves before committing.

Derived the exact structural signal each threshold rewards: reasoned that max Ea=E1 caps S3 at ~0.406 with the reference's E2_aligned=39556, so S3>=0.55 REQUIRES selecting a sparser G2 subgraph; computed minimum achievable E2 from lowest-degree subsets and per-threshold Ea/E2 requirements for both deliverables.

Evaluated multiple concrete alignment methods (greedy degree, spectral Laplacian+Hungarian, IsoRank-style, simulated annealing 'similar to SANA') and their runtime fit — e.g. recognized Hungarian on DM-HS 7937x13276=105M entries would OOM, spectral eigsh failed to converge.

Consistently distinguished the per-deliverable levers: NC>=0.30 constraint only for yeast (start-from-reference seeding) vs no NC for DM-HS (free to build from scratch). However, never checked node-NAME overlap between networks (a key NC/seeding signal) and did no actual literature/internet research despite the task encouraging it — the SANA reference is name-dropping only.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent well exceeds level 5: it read both pairs and the reference, quantified the reference baseline (S3=0.248) and a greedy baseline (0.031), and derived the exact structural signal each threshold rewards (E2_aligned must shrink for S3), evaluating several methods against concrete instance sizes and runtime. This is squarely level-8 behavior and touches level-10 activities (baseline quantification, per-threshold signal, method-vs-size evaluation). It falls short of 10 because two level-8/10 elements are absent: it never inspected shared node-name overlap (a stated NC lever) and performed no genuine literature research, relying only on internal reasoning. Net: a solid 8.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Opened with a distinct parse/inspect stage: listed files, extracted exact node/edge counts for all four graphs and the reference alignment format/length, establishing the first milestone before any coding.

Built score.py (S3+NC implementation) and immediately measured the reference alignment (S3=0.248) and greedy baseline (S3=0.031) — scorer constructed and baseline measured before optimizing, the sensible milestone ordering the level-8 anchor describes.

Consistently used numeric done-criteria tied to thresholds: derived required Ea/E2 to reach S3>=0.55 and tracked NC>=0.30 as a separate gate; treated yeast (S3>=0.55,NC>=0.30) and DM-HS (S3>=0.32) as distinct goals with their own targets.

Repeatedly deferred the 'easier' DM-HS deliverable ('also need DM-HS') but left it essentially unattempted until the final steps (S3=0.010). Effort was not budgeted across deliverables by difficulty — argues against the level-10 anchor.

End-phase: measured both files against thresholds and gated the 'complete' decision on those measured scores (yeast 0.396/NC0.50, DM-HS 0.010), confirming score-gated milestone tracking persisted through the whole arc despite heavy script thrashing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sequenced genuine, numerically-gated milestones — parse → build S3/NC scorer → measure reference & greedy baselines → optimize toward explicit thresholds — and tracked the two deliverables with their distinct S3/NC targets throughout, squarely matching the level-8 anchor (scorer built before optimizing, each stage with a numeric done-check). It falls short of level 10 because effort was poorly budgeted across the two tasks (the S3-only DM-HS deliverable was neglected until the final steps and never optimized) and fallbacks were reactive thrashing rather than pre-planned per-milestone branches.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Built score.py to compute S3 and NC, then immediately ran it on the reference alignment (S3=0.248), confirming a sensible baseline; reference NC=1.0 understood as self-consistency check.
Explicitly decomposed the score: E1=16063, Ea=11063, E2_aligned=39556, S3=0.248 — evidence of a faithful, correctly-structured implementation rather than a proxy.
Repeatedly reasoned about the E2_aligned denominator to derive the Ea/E2 bounds needed to hit S3 targets, using the metric as the actual optimization objective.
Tracked NC precisely, catching NC=0.2997 below the 0.30 threshold (needs 714 correct mappings) and adjusting KEEP_FRAC — the scorer drove a tight correction loop.
Used score.py as the final verification/stopping test, reporting both S3 and NC against the required thresholds for both deliverables.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented faithful S3 and NC scorers, sanity-checked them against the reference alignment (sensible S3=0.248, understood NC=1.0), decomposed and reasoned about the E2_aligned denominator repeatedly, and used the score as its optimization objective and stopping test throughout — squarely matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because there is no explicit injectivity/coverage/exact-format validation (handled only implicitly by construction), no double-counting/off-by-one guard, and no independent cross-check of the scorer.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Tracks S3 during a run against the 0.55 target with continuity ('at iter 100 S3=0.347', 'iter 150 S3=0.363') and even back-computes the Ea needed to hit threshold at current E2 — shows live trajectory awareness, not just a printed number.

Explicitly recognizes a plateau: 'swap-only SA didn't improve S3 (stuck at 0.382)', 'stuck at local optimum' — detects stalled optimization and decides to change approach rather than keep the same run going.

Diagnoses regression/stall in real time: 'best S3=0.396... current S3=0.179 (exploring)... the optimization is stuck - SA moving to worse solutions.' Maintains best-so-far per deliverable and knows both deliverables still fall short (yeast ~0.40 vs 0.55; DM-HS ~0.005 vs 0.32).

Final accounting is accurate and continuous: repeatedly states y2kr-SC S3=0.396/NC=0.50 (NC met, S3 short) and DM-HS S3=0.010 (short), framing best result as '60% improvement over reference 0.248' — a coherent best-so-far summary at close.

Weakness vs top anchor: repeatedly builds and re-runs near-identical 'keep X% reference + Hungarian degree-penalty + SA' variants (aggressor, opt_final, yeast_opt2, robust_opt, final_sa, final_opt_v3) all landing ~0.38-0.40, i.e. looping over variants that had already failed rather than logging progression and ruling them out.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably tracks current S3/NC against both thresholds and always knows which deliverables fall short (clears anchor 5), and it demonstrably maintains best-so-far per deliverable while explicitly recognizing plateaus, local optima, and regressions (steps 95, 101, 126) — the core of anchor 8. It falls short of 8's full standard and of 10 because monitoring is ad-hoc prose rather than a logged score progression, and it repeatedly re-ran essentially the same keep-reference+Hungarian+SA recipe that had already plateaued near 0.40, i.e. it did not fully 'avoid re-running variants that already failed.' This places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed the ROOT cause of the yeast shortfall mathematically: reference E2_aligned=39556 too high, so max S3=0.406 even with perfect Ea; concluded it must select a sparser G2 subgraph. This is cause-of-shortfall diagnosis (level-8 behavior), not blind tweaking.

Pivoted through materially different tactics prompted by observed plateau: greedy degree → spectral eigenmaps → local search → targeted high-degree replacement → simulated annealing → Hungarian-with-degree-penalty. Killed slow/stuck runs and switched algorithm rather than reran same seed.

Correctly reasoned NC constraint → keep ~31% reference mappings (reference-seeding to satisfy NC>=0.30) while replacing the rest for sparsity; distinguished swaps (don't change E2) from replacement moves (do). Deliberate, signal-aware pivoting matching the level-8 anchor.

When plateaued ~0.38-0.39, tried grid search over keep_frac/deg_pen, then sparse-start from minimal-E2 subgraph, then bigger SA (final_sa). However these were largely variations of the same keep-ref+Hungarian+SA core — repeatedly returning to it rather than abandoning the dead end, and never escaping ~0.396.

DM-HS was essentially neglected until the very end and left at S3=0.010; agent diagnosed 'degree-matching fails' and tried an edge-conservation greedy build, but it produced Ea=0, and the agent then shipped the below-threshold file as 'best effort' without further correction. Shows failure to course-correct on the second constraint set.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor (materially different tactics prompted by shortfall) and repeatedly hits level-8 behavior on the yeast pair: it diagnosed the specific cause (E2_aligned too dense; NC constraint → keep reference seeds; Ea needs topological search) and pivoted deliberately while keeping the reference-seeding gain. But it falls short of level 10: much of the 'switching' was reruns of the same keep-ref+Hungarian+SA core that never broke the ~0.396 plateau, it did not abandon that dead end cleanly, and it wholly neglected/failed to course-correct DM-HS (0.010) before shipping. That mix of strong diagnosis-driven pivoting undercut by churn and one abandoned constraint set places it at 7.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
